summary.text: A 27-year-old man with type 1 diabetes diagnosed 6 years earlier and self-discontinued insulin three weeks before admission developed 3 days of left-sided toothache and 9 hours of dyspnea, with Kussmaul respiration, dry mouth and vomiting. He presented in diabetic ketoacidosis (pH 6.996, glucose 22.2 mmol/L, lactate 2.7 mmol/L, urine ketones 3+).

After resuscitation with antibiotics, fluids and acidosis correction in the ICU he had mild dyspnea, intermittent chest tightness and marked left facial swelling. MRI showed a multispace infection of the floor of the mouth with cervical abscess, mediastinal extension and pleural effusion; the authors list deep cervical and mediastinal abscess among the diagnoses. On arrival in the operating theater he had pronounced maxillofacial swelling, severe trismus (interincisal distance <1.5 cm) and restricted cervical motion, with glucose 7 mmol/L.

Awake tracheostomy under local anesthesia was considered and abandoned; video-laryngoscope and supraglottic approaches were judged infeasible. Awake nasal fiberoptic tracheal intubation was done under intravenous dexmedetomidine and remifentanil sedation with sequential topical 2% lidocaine (total 150 mg) sprayed through an epidural catheter secured to a 3.5 mm bronchoscope without a working channel, preserving spontaneous ventilation.

General anesthesia (propofol, rocuronium, sufentanil; sevoflurane and remifentanil maintenance) was induced for incision and drainage of submental and sublingual abscesses and tracheostomy, completed within about 65 minutes with minimal blood loss; he went to the ICU on controlled mechanical ventilation.

He resumed spontaneous breathing on postoperative day 1 with 76 mL of drainage, received ceftriaxone sodium and linezolid, moved to a general ward on postoperative day 11 and was discharged in stable condition on postoperative day 21 with no signs of residual infection. No adverse events related to airway management or hypoxia, hemodynamic instability or discomfort during awake intubation were reported.
